title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-02-14
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch 1/2 Track at 15ips) -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a legendary Feb 14 1970 show with smoking Dark Star, The Eleven and Not Fade Away, plus an extra‑crispy mix.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this performance as one of the peak shows of the Dead’s early ’70 era – the electric set delivers a monster Dark Star, explosive post‑drums jams and tight renditions of The Eleven, St. Stephen and Lovelight, while the acoustic half shines on Dark Hollow and Uncle John’s.  Charlie Miller’s remastered soundboard is praised as “extra crispy” and remarkably clear despite a few unavoidable cuts in the early set.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed, overwhelmingly positive reviews praise both musical performance and audio fidelity; the weighting of show quality (70 %) and recording quality (30 %) yields an elite rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered, normalized and re‑pitched by Charlie Miller – crisp, balanced mix with “extra crispy” clarity.  The only drawbacks are missing portions of the early set (beginning of The Eleven and a William Tell bridge in St. Stephen).

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑show marathon – an early acoustic set that builds into a fiery electric second set, followed by a third “continuous” set with seamless segues; reviewers note the post‑drums explosion and tight band interplay throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for fluid, soaring lead work and perfect tone; his solo sections are described as ‘orbiting’ and ‘arabesque’.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is mentioned briefly as solid and supportive; no major complaints.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers (Kreutzmann & Hart) receive high marks – the post‑drums section is called “explosive” and “on point”.
